passages.text: Thus King Darius ordered a search of the archives stored in the treasury of Babylon.
passages.sermon:
King Darius was the ruler at this time.
King Darius gave a command.
He ordered his officials to search the archives.
These archives were stored in the treasury of Babylon.
passages.original: בֵּאדַ֛יִן דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א שָׂ֣ם טְעֵ֑ם וּבַקַּ֣רוּ׀ בְּבֵ֣ית סִפְרַיָּ֗א דִּ֧י גִנְזַיָּ֛א מְהַחֲתִ֥ין תַּמָּ֖ה בְּבָבֶֽל׃

passages.text: And a scroll was found in the fortress of Ecbatana, in the province of Media, with the following written on it: Memorandum: In the first year of King Cyrus, he issued a decree concerning the house of God in Jerusalem: Let the house be rebuilt as a place for offering sacrifices, and let its foundations be firmly laid. It is to be sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide, with three layers of cut stones and one of timbers. The costs are to be paid from the royal treasury.
passages.sermon:
A scroll was found in the fortress of Ecbatana.
Ecbatana is in the province of Media.
The scroll contained a memorandum.
The memorandum recorded a decree from King Cyrus.
King Cyrus gave this decree in his first year as king.
The decree concerned the house of God in Jerusalem.
King Cyrus commanded that the house of God in Jerusalem must be rebuilt.
The house must be a place for offering sacrifices.
The foundations of the house must be firmly laid.
The house must be sixty cubits high.
The house must be sixty cubits wide.
The builders must use three layers of cut stones.
They must use one layer of timbers.
The royal treasury must pay the costs.
passages.original: וְהִשְׁתְּכַ֣ח בְּאַחְמְתָ֗א בְּבִֽירְתָ֛א דִּ֛י בְּמָדַ֥י מְדִינְתָּ֖ה מְגִלָּ֣ה חֲדָ֑ה וְכֵן־ כְּתִ֥יב בְּגַוַּ֖הּ דִּכְרוֹנָֽה׃פ בִּשְׁנַ֨ת חֲדָ֜ה לְכ֣וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֗א כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּא֮ שָׂ֣ם טְעֵם֒ בֵּית־ אֱלָהָ֤א בִֽירוּשְׁלֶם֙ בַּיְתָ֣א יִתְבְּנֵ֔א אֲתַר֙ דִּֽי־ דָבְחִ֣ין דִּבְחִ֔ין וְאֻשּׁ֖וֹהִי מְסֽוֹבְלִ֑ין רוּמֵהּ֙ אַמִּ֣ין שִׁתִּ֔ין פְּתָיֵ֖הּ אַמִּ֥ין שִׁתִּֽין׃ נִדְבָּכִ֞ין דִּי־ אֶ֤בֶן גְּלָל֙ תְּלָתָ֔א וְנִדְבָּ֖ךְ דִּי־ אָ֣ע חֲדַ֑ת וְנִ֨פְקְתָ֔א מִן־ בֵּ֥ית מַלְכָּ֖א תִּתְיְהִֽב׃

passages.text: Furthermore, the gold and silver articles of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and carried to Babylon, must also be returned to the temple in Jerusalem and deposited in the house of God.
passages.sermon:
King Darius gave a command.
He spoke about the gold and silver articles.
These articles belonged to the house of God in Jerusalem.
Nebuchadnezzar took these articles from the temple in Jerusalem.
Nebuchadnezzar carried them to Babylon.
Now, these articles must be returned.
They must go back to the temple in Jerusalem.
They must be placed in the house of God.
They must be put in their proper place.
passages.original: וְ֠אַף מָאנֵ֣י בֵית־ אֱלָהָא֮ דִּ֣י דַהֲבָ֣ה וְכַסְפָּא֒ דִּ֣י נְבֽוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר הַנְפֵּ֛ק מִן־ הֵיכְלָ֥א דִי־ בִירוּשְׁלֶ֖ם וְהֵיבֵ֣ל לְבָבֶ֑ל יַהֲתִיב֗וּן וִ֠יהָךְ לְהֵיכְלָ֤א דִי־ בִירֽוּשְׁלֶם֙ לְאַתְרֵ֔הּ וְתַחֵ֖ת בְּבֵ֥ית אֱלָהָֽא׃ס

passages.text: Therefore Darius decreed: To Tattenai governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and your associates and officials in the region: You must stay away from that place!
passages.sermon:
King Darius gave a command.
He spoke to Tattenai.
Tattenai was the governor west of the Euphrates River.
He spoke to Shethar-bozenai.
He spoke to their associates and officials in that region.
He told them to stay away from Jerusalem.
He told them not to interfere with the work there.
passages.original: כְּעַ֡ן תַּ֠תְּנַי פַּחַ֨ת עֲבַֽר־ נַהֲרָ֜ה שְׁתַ֤ר בּוֹזְנַי֙ וּכְנָוָ֣תְה֔וֹן אֲפַרְסְכָיֵ֔א דִּ֖י בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֑ה רַחִיקִ֥ין הֲו֖וֹ מִן־ תַּמָּֽה׃

passages.text: Leave this work on the house of God alone. Let the governor and elders of the Jews rebuild this house of God on its original site.
passages.sermon:
King Darius gave a command.
He spoke to the officials west of the Euphrates River.
He spoke to Tattenai, the governor.
He spoke to Shethar-bozenai and their associates.
He told them to stay away from the temple in Jerusalem.
He said, “Do not interfere with the work on the house of God.”
He said, “Let the governor of the Jews continue the work.”
He said, “Let the elders of the Jews rebuild the house of God.”
He said, “Let them build it on its original site.”
passages.original: שְׁבֻ֕קוּ לַעֲבִידַ֖ת בֵּית־ אֱלָהָ֣א דֵ֑ךְ פַּחַ֤ת יְהוּדָיֵא֙ וּלְשָׂבֵ֣י יְהוּדָיֵ֔א בֵּית־ אֱלָהָ֥א דֵ֖ךְ יִבְנ֥וֹן עַל־ אַתְרֵֽהּ׃

passages.text: I hereby decree what you must do for these elders of the Jews who are rebuilding this house of God: The cost is to be paid in full to these men from the royal treasury out of the taxes of the provinces west of the Euphrates, so that the work will not be hindered.
passages.sermon:
King Darius gave a command.
He spoke to the officials west of the Euphrates River.
He spoke about the elders of the Jews.
These elders are rebuilding the house of God.
You must help these elders.
You must pay all the costs for this work.
You must use money from the royal treasury.
This money comes from the taxes collected in your provinces west of the Euphrates.
You must give this money to the Jewish elders.
You must not let the work stop.
You must not hinder the building of the house of God.
passages.original: וּמִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ לְמָ֣א דִֽי־ תַֽעַבְד֗וּן עִם־ שָׂבֵ֤י יְהוּדָיֵא֙ אִלֵּ֔ךְ לְמִבְנֵ֖א בֵּית־ אֱלָהָ֣א דֵ֑ךְ וּמִנִּכְסֵ֣י מַלְכָּ֗א דִּ֚י מִדַּת֙ עֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֔ה אָסְפַּ֗רְנָא נִפְקְתָ֛א תֶּהֱוֵ֧א מִֽתְיַהֲבָ֛א לְגֻבְרַיָּ֥א אִלֵּ֖ךְ דִּי־ לָ֥א לְבַטָּלָֽא׃

passages.text: Whatever is needed—young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and oil, as requested by the priests in Jerusalem—must be given to them daily without fail.
passages.sermon:
King Darius gave a command about the temple in Jerusalem.
The Jews were rebuilding the house of God.
The priests in Jerusalem needed supplies for worship.
They needed young bulls, rams, and lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven.
They also needed wheat, salt, wine, and oil.
The priests would say what they needed.
The people must give these things to the priests every day.
They must not fail to give what is needed.
passages.original: וּמָ֣ה חַשְׁחָ֡ן וּבְנֵ֣י תוֹרִ֣ין וְדִכְרִ֣ין וְאִמְּרִ֣ין׀ לַעֲלָוָ֣ן׀ לֶאֱלָ֪הּ שְׁמַיָּ֟א חִנְטִ֞ין מְלַ֣ח׀ חֲמַ֣ר וּמְשַׁ֗ח כְּמֵאמַ֨ר כָּהֲנַיָּ֤א דִי־ בִירֽוּשְׁלֶם֙ לֶהֱוֵ֨א מִתְיְהֵ֥ב לְהֹ֛ם י֥וֹם׀ בְּי֖וֹם דִּי־ לָ֥א שָׁלֽוּ׃

passages.text: Then they will be able to offer sacrifices of a sweet aroma to the God of heaven and to pray for the lives of the king and his sons.
passages.sermon:
The elders of the Jews are rebuilding the house of God in Jerusalem.
They receive everything they need each day.
They offer sacrifices to the God of heaven.
These sacrifices have a pleasing aroma.
They pray for the life of the king.
They pray for the lives of the king’s sons.
passages.original: דִּֽי־ לֶהֱוֺ֧ן מְהַקְרְבִ֛ין נִיחוֹחִ֖ין לֶאֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֑א וּמְצַלַּ֕יִן לְחַיֵּ֥י מַלְכָּ֖א וּבְנֽוֹהִי׃

passages.text: I also decree that if any man interferes with this directive, a beam is to be torn from his house and raised up, and he is to be impaled on it. And his own house shall be made a pile of rubble for this offense.
passages.sermon:
King Darius gave a decree.
He said this law must not be changed or opposed.
If any person tries to change this command, punish him.
Take a beam from his house.
Set up the beam.
Impale him on the beam.
Make his house a heap of ruins because of this offense.
passages.original: וּמִנִּי֮ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵם֒ דִּ֣י כָל־ אֱנָ֗שׁ דִּ֤י יְהַשְׁנֵא֙ פִּתְגָמָ֣א דְנָ֔ה יִתְנְסַ֥ח אָע֙ מִן־ בַּיְתֵ֔הּ וּזְקִ֖יף יִתְמְחֵ֣א עֲלֹ֑הִי וּבַיְתֵ֛הּ נְוָל֥וּ יִתְעֲבֵ֖ד עַל־ דְּנָֽה׃

passages.text: May God, who has caused His Name to dwell there, overthrow any king or people who lifts a hand to alter this decree or to destroy this house of God in Jerusalem. I, Darius, have issued the decree. Let it be carried out with diligence.
passages.sermon:
God has caused His Name to dwell in Jerusalem.
God lives there.
May God overthrow any king who tries to change this decree.
May God overthrow any people who tries to destroy the house of God in Jerusalem.
I am Darius.
I have issued this decree.
Carry out this decree with diligence.
passages.original: וֵֽאלָהָ֞א דִּ֣י שַׁכִּ֧ן שְׁמֵ֣הּ תַּמָּ֗ה יְמַגַּ֞ר כָּל־ מֶ֤לֶךְ וְעַם֙ דִּ֣י׀ יִשְׁלַ֣ח יְדֵ֗הּ לְהַשְׁנָיָ֛ה לְחַבָּלָ֛ה בֵּית־ אֱלָהָ֥א דֵ֖ךְ דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם אֲנָ֤ה דָרְיָ֙וֶשׁ֙ שָׂ֣מֶת טְעֵ֔ם אָסְפַּ֖רְנָא יִתְעֲבִֽד׃פ

passages.text: In response, Tattenai the governor of the region west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates diligently carried out what King Darius had decreed.
passages.sermon:
Tattenai was the governor of the region west of the Euphrates.
Shethar-bozenai worked with him.
Their associates also helped them.
King Darius sent a decree.
Tattenai, Shethar-bozenai, and their associates obeyed the decree.
They carried out everything King Darius commanded.
They did this diligently.
passages.original: אֱ֠דַיִן תַּתְּנַ֞י פַּחַ֧ת עֲבַֽר־ נַהֲרָ֛ה שְׁתַ֥ר בּוֹזְנַ֖י וּכְנָוָתְה֑וֹן לָקֳבֵ֗ל דִּֽי־ שְׁלַ֞ח דָּרְיָ֧וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֛א כְּנֵ֖מָא אָסְפַּ֥רְנָא עֲבַֽדוּ׃

passages.text: So the Jewish elders built and prospered through the prophesying of Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo. They finished building according to the command of the God of Israel and the decrees of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia.
passages.sermon:
The Jewish elders led the people.
They built the temple in Jerusalem.
They succeeded in their work.
Haggai was a prophet.
Zechariah, son of Iddo, was also a prophet.
Haggai and Zechariah spoke God’s word to the people.
The people listened to these prophets.
The people prospered because of the prophets’ messages.
God of Israel commanded the people to build the temple.
Cyrus, king of Persia, gave a decree to build the temple.
Darius, king of Persia, also gave a decree.
Artaxerxes, king of Persia, gave a decree as well.
The people finished building the temple.
They obeyed the command of God and the decrees of the Persian kings.
passages.original: וְשָׂבֵ֤י יְהוּדָיֵא֙ בָּנַ֣יִן וּמַצְלְחִ֔ין בִּנְבוּאַת֙ חַגַּ֣י נְבִיאָה וּזְכַרְיָ֖ה בַּר־ עִדּ֑וֹא וּבְנ֣וֹ וְשַׁכְלִ֗לוּ מִן־ טַ֙עַם֙ אֱלָ֣הּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וּמִטְּעֵם֙ כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ וְדָרְיָ֔וֶשׁ וְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֖שְׂתְּא מֶ֥לֶךְ פָּרָֽס׃

passages.text: And this temple was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
passages.sermon:
The Jews rebuilt the temple in Jerusalem.
They finished the work.
They completed the temple on the third day of the month of Adar.
This happened in the sixth year of King Darius’s reign.
passages.original: וְשֵׁיצִיא֙ בַּיְתָ֣ה דְנָ֔ה עַ֛ד י֥וֹם תְּלָתָ֖ה לִירַ֣ח אֲדָ֑ר דִּי־ הִ֣יא שְׁנַת־ שֵׁ֔ת לְמַלְכ֖וּת דָּרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּֽא׃פ

passages.text: Then the people of Israel—the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the exiles—celebrated the dedication of the house of God with joy.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel gathered together.
The priests were there.
The Levites were there.
The rest of the exiles were there.
They dedicated the house of God.
They celebrated with joy.
passages.original: וַעֲבַ֣דוּ בְנֵֽי־ יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל כָּהֲנַיָּ֨א וְלֵוָיֵ֜א וּשְׁאָ֣ר בְּנֵי־ גָלוּתָ֗א חֲנֻכַּ֛ת בֵּית־ אֱלָהָ֥א דְנָ֖ה בְּחֶדְוָֽה׃

passages.text: For the dedication of the house of God they offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and a sin offering for all Israel of twelve male goats, one for each tribe of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The people of Israel dedicated the house of God.
They brought offerings for this dedication.
They offered one hundred bulls.
They offered two hundred rams.
They offered four hundred lambs.
They gave twelve male goats as a sin offering for all Israel.
They gave one goat for each tribe of Israel.
There are twelve tribes in Israel.
passages.original: וְהַקְרִ֗בוּ לַחֲנֻכַּת֮ בֵּית־ אֱלָהָ֣א דְנָה֒ תּוֹרִ֣ין מְאָ֔ה דִּכְרִ֣ין מָאתַ֔יִן אִמְּרִ֖ין אַרְבַּ֣ע מְאָ֑ה וּצְפִירֵ֨י עִזִּ֜ין לְחַטָּיָא עַל־ כָּל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ תְּרֵֽי־ עֲשַׂ֔ר לְמִנְיָ֖ן שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: They also appointed the priests by their divisions and the Levites by their groups to the service of God in Jerusalem, according to what is written in the Book of Moses.
passages.sermon:
The leaders appointed the priests.
They put each priest into his own division.
They appointed the Levites.
They put each Levite into his own group.
The priests and Levites served God in Jerusalem.
They did everything as the Book of Moses commands.
passages.original: וַהֲקִ֨ימוּ כָהֲנַיָּ֜א בִּפְלֻגָּתְה֗וֹן וְלֵוָיֵא֙ בְּמַחְלְקָ֣תְה֔וֹן עַל־ עֲבִידַ֥ת אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם כִּכְתָ֖ב סְפַ֥ר מֹשֶֽׁה׃פ

passages.text: On the fourteenth day of the first month, the exiles kept the Passover.
passages.sermon: The exiles were Israelites who had returned from captivity.\r\nThey kept the Passover.\r\nThey did this on the fourteenth day of the first month.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲשׂ֥וּ בְנֵי־ הַגּוֹלָ֖ה אֶת־ הַפָּ֑סַח בְּאַרְבָּעָ֥ה עָשָׂ֖ר לַחֹ֥דֶשׁ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: All the priests and Levites had purified themselves and were ceremonially clean. And the Levites slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the exiles, for their priestly brothers, and for themselves.
passages.sermon:
The priests and the Levites served God in Jerusalem.
All the priests purified themselves.
All the Levites purified themselves.
They did this together.
Now every priest and every Levite was clean.
The Levites slaughtered the Passover lamb.
They did this for all the exiles.
They did this for their fellow priests.
They did this for themselves.
passages.original: כִּ֣י הִֽטַּהֲר֞וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֧ים וְהַלְוִיִּ֛ם כְּאֶחָ֖ד כֻּלָּ֣ם טְהוֹרִ֑ים וַיִּשְׁחֲט֤וּ הַפֶּ֙סַח֙ לְכָל־ בְּנֵ֣י הַגּוֹלָ֔ה וְלַאֲחֵיהֶ֥ם הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים וְלָהֶֽם׃

passages.text: The Israelites who had returned from exile ate it, together with all who had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land to seek the LORD, the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites had returned from exile.
They ate the Passover meal.
Others joined them.
These others had separated themselves from the uncleanness of the peoples of the land.
They did this to seek the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
passages.original: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ בְנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַשָּׁבִים֙ מֵֽהַגּוֹלָ֔ה וְכֹ֗ל הַנִּבְדָּ֛ל מִטֻּמְאַ֥ת גּוֹיֵֽ־ הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם לִדְרֹ֕שׁ לַֽיהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For seven days they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread with joy, because the LORD had made them joyful and turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward them to strengthen their hands in the work on the house of the God of Israel.
passages.sermon:
The Israelites had returned from exile.
They celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
They were joyful during the feast.
The LORD made them joyful.
The LORD turned the heart of the king of Assyria toward the Israelites.
The king of Assyria supported them.
He strengthened their hands.
They worked on the house of the God of Israel.
passages.original: וַיַּֽעֲשׂ֧וּ חַג־ מַצּ֛וֹת שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים בְּשִׂמְחָ֑ה כִּ֣י׀ שִׂמְּחָ֣ם יְהוָ֗ה וְֽהֵסֵ֞ב לֵ֤ב מֶֽלֶךְ־ אַשּׁוּר֙ עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם לְחַזֵּ֣ק יְדֵיהֶ֔ם בִּמְלֶ֥אכֶת בֵּית־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֱלֹהֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃פ
